author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell walked through why the Transfiguration means so much to him, the moment Christ takes Peter, John, and James up a mountain to pray, right after warning them, again, that he would die and be resurrected, a truth they still couldn't fully grasp. As he prayed, his face changed and his clothes turned dazzling white, joined by Moses and Elijah discussing his coming death in Jerusalem. Russell reflected on the poetic and symbolic layers of the story, careful to note this isn't skepticism about what actually happened, but recognition that God lived out a truth so permanent it would outlast time itself, something meant to be recognized rather than merely witnessed.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Before Christ, Russell says he believed God was real, even the ultimate reality itself, though he leaned on C.S. Lewis's point that most people's image of God as a father figure isn't much more sophisticated than imagining Santa Claus. He admitted his appetite for worship was always enormous, enough to sense the world could never satisfy it, but what stayed hidden from him for years was that he'd actually been worshipping himself, something he never suspected precisely because he didn't like himself very much. Russell was honest about why he avoided Christianity for so long, finding it bloody boring growing up, joking that hearing "the Lord of the dance" made him want to give up on the spot. He's since explored many different expressions of the faith, but still sees the same challenge facing Christianity that he's noticed in recovery programs, the danger of nestling too comfortably inside a dominant culture he considers fundamentally fallen.

author: Russell Brand
description:
A clip broke down how often AOC invokes her Bronx identity, repeating it again this week while responding to President Trump, and questioned why any functional adult would need to repeat where they're from quite so often, framing it as a common tell of dishonesty. The clip claims that despite the persona, her family has actually lived in Yorktown Heights, a well off, quiet hamlet, since she was an infant, a stark contrast to the working class image being projected. Russell closes out the segment with his own take, questioning why politicians so consistently claim backgrounds just like everyone else's, whether or not it holds up.

description:
Before the pandemic, Fauci reportedly directed millions in taxpayer funding toward gain of function research on bat coronaviruses at the Wuhan Institute of Virology, information Russell notes was conspicuously absent from his early pandemic messaging, which focused instead on masks and vaccines. Newly released communications reportedly expose how he worked with politicized intelligence leadership to suppress information about his own role and the virus's possible lab origins. Russell recalled the surreal cultural moment at the time, Fauci being celebrated, even treated as a kind of sex symbol, with interviewers gushing over his workout routine while the real questions went unasked. Now, facing renewed scrutiny, Russell wonders whether today might finally bring the reckoning that's been missing for years, though he admits he's not holding his breath.
